back: Row-major (CSV): fast row reads and appends. Column-major (Parquet): fast reads of a few columns.
Batch: periodic jobs on historical data (static features). Stream: computation on data in flight with low delay and stateful updates (dynamic features).
Keep the first $k$ items; for item $n>k$ draw $j\sim U\{1..n\}$ and replace slot $j$ if $j\le k$.
New item enters with $k/(n+1)$; an old one survives with $n/(n+1)$; product with $k/n$ gives $k/(n+1)$.
Sample each group (stratum) separately so rare groups are represented; hard when items have several labels.
$P(x)/Q(x)$ for a sample drawn from proposal $Q$ to estimate under $P$.
Convenience, snowball, judgement and quota sampling; cheap but biased.
Labels from system feedback such as clicks or actual arrival times; they arrive with a delay called the feedback loop length.
Expensive, slow, a privacy risk, and annotators disagree.
A small program encoding a heuristic that votes for a class or abstains; outputs are noisy and may conflict.

front: Weight of a labelling function in a weighted vote
back: $w=\log\frac{a}{1-a}$ for accuracy $a$; vote $+w$ for class 1, $-w$ for class 0.
Extend labels by structure or self-training; start from a pretrained model; choose which examples to label by uncertainty.
Transformations that keep the label (flip, crop, synonym swap); apply to the training split only.
Little signal for the rare class, a trivial majority-class shortcut, and costly errors on the rare class. See cml.11.
